stem: Which facial feature combination is most suggestive of foetal alcohol syndrome?

options.text: Smooth philtrum and thin upper lip

explanation: Smooth philtrum and thin upper lip are the facial features most suggestive of foetal alcohol syndrome.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Foetal alcohol syndrome has a characteristic facial appearance, and a smooth philtrum with a thin upper lip is a key clue. The other options describe features associated with different genetic or neurocutaneous syndromes.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a smooth philtrum and thin upper lip are classic facial features of foetal alcohol syndrome.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because long ears and hypermobility are more suggestive of Fragile X syndrome.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because coloboma and ear abnormalities are associated with CHARGE syndrome.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because ashleaf spots and shagreen patches are features of tuberous sclerosis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because cafe-au-lait spots and neurofibromas are features of neurofibromatosis type 1.
